title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཟེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 191)
shelf_note: A Derge woodblock folio of Pramāṇa verse. The page discusses upamāna (comparison): the gavaya/cow example, why it is neither perception nor inference, and the dispute over whether universals are real. That matches the Tattvasaṃgraha material in Tshad ma ze.

ocr_errors.image: Line 7 reads most like དམ་བཅའི་དོན་དང་ཡུལ་གཅིག་ཉིད (compare the earlier དམ་བཅའི་དོན་དང་ཡུལ་གཅིག་ཕྱིར), but the image is not clear at this resolution
ocr_errors.problem: Possible misread of the particle (དུ for དང); the meaning barely changes

ocr_errors.image: The last syllables of the folio look like བ་མེན་, the spelling used elsewhere on the page
ocr_errors.problem: Possible spelling normalisation at the page end

tr_errors_A.english: because it shares the same sphere of reference with the thesis
tr_errors_A.problem: ཡུལ་གཅིག here renders ekadeśa ('a part of the thesis'), not 'same sphere'. The reason is blurred, though the argument can still be followed

tr_errors_A.english: If one objects: because the object of comprehension lacks real existence, this is not accepted as a valid instrument
tr_errors_A.problem: The Tibetan has no 'if one objects' marker. Adding one frames this statement as an opponent's objection rather than a plain assertion

tr_errors_A.english: the cognition of similarity that arises regarding that wild cattle
tr_errors_A.problem: 'Wild cattle' for ཕྱུགས is an interpretive rendering; acceptable

tr_errors_B.english: is it not the case that it becomes the object of a distinguished valid cognition of inference
tr_errors_B.problem: The source says inference is not a non-pramāṇa because its object is qualified. B turns this into a garbled rhetorical question about 'becoming the object of' inference. The point is still recoverable

tr_errors_B.english: any consciousness that arises as a similarity to that cow is exemplified by the form of the ox
tr_errors_B.problem: The roles are muddled: the similarity is said to be 'to that cow', and the cow-form example becomes 'the ox'

tr_errors_B.english: because the object and the subject of the thesis are the same
tr_errors_B.problem: Misreads ekadeśa ('a part of the thesis') as an identity of object and subject

tr_errors_B.english: If one asks how there can be a connection of similarity through many common parts
tr_errors_B.problem: The source is a claim ('if you say there is a similarity…'). B turns it into a question

tr_errors_B.english: gayal <gloss>a wild ox-like animal, Bos gaurus</gloss>
tr_errors_B.problem: The gloss gives the wrong species: Bos gaurus is the gaur, while the gayal is Bos frontalis

pages.prefer_reason: Neither version has a serious error, but A renders the inference-is-a-pramāṇa parallel and the cow/gavaya example correctly, where B garbles both and also gets the gavaya gloss wrong.

book_verdict: A clean Derge Pramāṇa folio on upamāna. The transcription is close to the block print. Both English versions are serviceable; A is the more faithful.
